algorithm_steps: Inputs are finite stored-real standard-form LP data, full-row-rank A with rank preprocessing supplied, a valid ordered initial basis, finite basis-replacement proposal list of length L, evaluation budget K>=0 and optional nonnegative residual thresholds. Each proposed replacement is one leaving position and one currently nonbasic column; retain all existing exact primal/dual/PhaseI methods. An existing exact driver may supply its exact legal basis sequence; a numerical proposal is not automatically a valid simplex pivot.

Process at most min(L+1,K) basis states, including initial basis. Validate dimensions/finiteness/distinct indices and the declared nonsingularity of each input basis. For a proposed replacement whose nonsingularity cannot be established, return basis-validity-inconclusive, retaining the last audited basis. No numerical rank tolerance declares an exact singular or infeasible LP.

For m>=1, factor C=A_B and C^T separately from current original stored columns using the canonical scaled Householder QR sequence. Apply stored reflectors by the analyzed rounded rank-one updates (never treat a rounded dense Q as exactly orthogonal), then successful rounded triangular substitution for C*xhat_B=b, C^T*yhat=c_B and C*dhat_j=a_j for each requested nonbasic direction. Reuse a same-basis factorization for separate RHS; after every basis replacement discard it and recompute both QR factorizations from current stored A_B. This is the approved recomputation branch of basis updates, not a newly implemented factorization/update scheme.

All calls retain the operationwise no-underflow/normal/finite/range checks, 0<u<1, mu<1, (m+3)u<1 and gamma_(m+3)<1/8. Failed factorization/substitution/residual evaluation/certificate arithmetic returns numerical-failure with exact stage and last successful audit. The m=0 branch uses no QR: empty x_B,y,d, zero basis-equation residuals and the existing exact empty-basis audit.

For each successful solve Cz=r or C^T z=r, compute vhat=fl(Cz), what=fl(vhat-r) by successful sequential dots/subtraction. With g_m=(1+6u)/(1-(m-1)u)-1 set W=g_m||C||F||zhat||2+u(||vhat||2+||r||2). Let beta=(1+kappa_m)^m-1 and beta_C=beta+gamma_(m+3)(1+beta). Return eta=min{||what||2+W,beta_C||C||F||zhat||2+beta||r||2}, using exact norms or certified upward bounds for both branches. Apply identical formula to C^T. A larger validated bound is legal; if no finite certified bound is available, no certificate is returned.

Embed xhat_B with zero nonbasic entries and invoke alg-revised-simplex-residual-audit on the actual stored xhat,yhat. Return basis and each solve residual bound, exact stored-data primal residual/slack/objective gap and the existing audit status. If supplied basis thresholds are met, basis-solves-residual-certified means only those inequalities. The exact audit alone may issue verified-optimal-for-stored-data under its exact primal/sign/gap checks. Otherwise return candidate-only or budget-exhausted, not approximate optimality/infeasibility.

A proposed replacement without separately validated simplex sign/ratio premises is a basis proposal only. This service does not assert exact Bland pivots, primal/dual feasibility invariants or no-cycling from floating signs. If attached to the existing exact driver, legal pivot/basis claims remain those of that driver, while this service supplies the computed candidate/status layer. Forward error of each basis solve is at most ||C^-1||2*eta (and transpose analog); signs/ratios require an actual certified inverse-norm/interval bound or exact existing pivot checks. Unavailable or overlapping sign/ratio validation must return pivot-inconclusive, not silently choose an exact certified pivot. No guaranteed numerical success or polynomial-time claim.
proof_route: Every call has finite dimensions/loops and finite budget. Canonical arithmetic returns a finite result or first failure; exact rational audit of finite dyadic input terminates. Basis replacement increments the counted state and discards stale factors, so at most min(L+1,K) states are audited. m=0 is direct finite arithmetic.

For square nonsingular C, the source1 QR/triangular equations yield C+Delta_Q=Qhat Rhat and (Rhat+Delta_R)zhat=Qhat^T(r+delta r). Qhat is square and exactly orthogonal as represented, so multiplying gives (C+Delta_C)zhat=r+delta r, Delta_C=Delta_Q+Qhat Delta_R. Hence ||Delta_C||F<=beta_C||C||F and ||Czhat-r||2<=beta_C||C||F||zhat||2+beta||r||2. No nonsingularity of Rhat+Delta_R is needed for this residual conclusion; successful substitution and actual C nonsingularity suffice.

The rounded residual lemma bounds ||what-(Czhat-r)||2<=W. Triangle inequality gives the other candidate bound. Both entries are upper bounds, so their minimum is an upper bound. Repeat for every RHS and C^T; failure grants no certificate.

The existing exact audit gives g=xhat^T r_d+yhat^T r_p and |g|<=||xhat||1||r_d||infinity+||yhat||1||r_p||infinity for the stored data. Only its exact primal feasibility, dual slack nonnegativity and zero gap imply stored-data optimality. A small residual neither implies a small solution error without inverse norm nor validates signs/ratios or pre-rounded input data.

Recomputation ties each returned certificate to the actual current C and RHS. Conditional exact driver transitions preserve their already-proved mathematical properties; arbitrary finite basis proposals are not asserted to do so. Every failure or ambiguity keeps the last audited candidate and explicit inconclusive status.
